claims.text: HfMoNbTaTiZr is a refractory BCC high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast HfMoNbTaTiZr baseline has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
The as-cast baseline contains no secondary precipitates.
Minor boron addition followed by tailored heat treatment will induce in situ boride precipitation.
The induced boride precipitates will be fine and stable at elevated temperature.
The borides will form a uniformly dispersed network at grain boundaries and within grains.
The boride precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion at high temperature.
The boride precipitates will inhibit grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Boron addition and boride precipitation will increase elevated-temperature yield strength relative to the undoped baseline.
Boron addition and boride precipitation will improve creep resistance relative to the undoped baseline.
The proposed improvement should hold at temperatures at or above 800 °C.
The proposed alloy modification is applicable to high-temperature aerospace components.
The proposed alloy modification is applicable to high-temperature nuclear-reactor service.
The magnitude of strengthening and the optimal boron concentration and heat treatment depend on processing details and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome describe comparison with an undoped as-cast alloy, whereas the baseline and conditions require an undoped control receiving the same heat-treatment route. These are materially different baselines.
